newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danske Bank content with '96, wary on '97.
newsitem.headline: Danske Bank content with '96, wary on '97.

text.p: Den Danske Bank, Denmark's biggest banking group, on Thursday said it was not disappointed with its full year 1996 result but warned that there would be little growth in core earnings in 1997.
"The year's result is fairly satisfactory as far as I can see," Danske Bank chief executive Knud Soerensen said in a statement accompanying the 1996 result.

Den Danske Bank earlier posted pre-tax and extraordinary items profits of 5.396 billion crowns, lower than 1995's 6.034 billion crowns but better than average analyst expectations of 4.800 billion crowns.
But the bank said it did not see operating costs falling in 1997, adding that core earnings would grow only modestly if at all this year.
"The board does not see costs falling in 1997 and it is also uncertain if the current losses and bad debt provision level can be maintained," Den Danske Bank said.
"Little or no improvement in core earnings is foreseen and any income here would not be sufficient to ensure a satisfactory return on the bank's considerable capital," it said.

"Despite tight cost controls, including staff reductions, the bank's costs are not expected to fall. This is due to the expense of introducing new information technology and increasing activity in the Nordic region, including the running costs of three branches there," the bank said.

Losses and bad debt provisions fell to 637 million crowns in 1996 from the previous year's 1.254 billion crowns, while the bank's core earnings including insurance activities rose last year to 3.730 billion crowns from 2.785 billion crowns.
Den Danske Bank's operating costs in 1996 fell marginally to 5.741 billion crowns from the previous year's 5.814 billion.
